content_units: For your priorities—  fewer layovers first, then total travel time, then price  —the best pick is   Option A  .
Your backup is   Option D   if you want the most convenient nonstop trip with extra inclusions and are comfortable paying more.
Airline   Departure   Arrival   Duration   Stops   Fare
Option A   2026-05-12 6:55 PM   2026-05-13 5:50 AM   6h 55m outbound / 7h 40m return   Non-stop   USD 742
Option D   2026-05-12 6:55 PM   2026-05-13 5:50 AM   Non-stop both ways   Non-stop   USD 801
Option C   2026-05-12 6:55 PM   2026-05-13 5:50 AM   6h 55m outbound / 10h 50m return   1 stop return   USD 688
Option B   2026-05-12 6:55 PM   2026-05-13 6:15 AM   11h 20m outbound / 12h 05m return   1 stop each way   USD 615
-   Meets your top priority perfectly:   nonstop both directions
- Only   $54 more than C   for avoiding a return layover
- Only   $127 more than B   for saving several hours and both connection risks
- Includes   checked bag   and   seat selection
- Best if those extras would otherwise cost close to the   $59 difference vs A
- Not the top pick because your priorities put   stops and travel time ahead of extras  , and A already matches D on those core factors
- Better than B because it has   only one layover total
- Loses to A because A avoids that return connection entirely
- Good value if you want to save   $54 vs A   and can accept a slower return
- Cheapest, but weakest for your stated priorities
-   One stop each way   plus much longer total travel time
- Best only if price suddenly becomes your main concern
-   A vs D:   tie on layovers; A likely wins on value because it is cheaper
-   A vs C:   A wins because   0 total layover flights on both legs   beats a mixed nonstop/1-stop itinerary
-   A vs B:   A wins easily on both stops and time
